Executive Summary This repository houses the complete design, configuration, and verification for an enterprise-scale secure network infrastructure built using **FortiGate Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW)** and **Cisco IOS Routers & Switches**. The project simulates a distributed corporate organization composed of: 1. **Corporate Headquarters (HQ):** Dual FortiGate NGFWs running Active-Passive High Availability (HA), Cisco Core distribution switch, and dedicated access switches isolating 5 micro-segmented VLAN tiers. 2. **Branch 1 (BR1):** Dedicated FortiGate perimeter with local user and server VLAN segmentation. 3. **Branch 2 (BR2):** Redundant branch perimeter providing local LAN segmentation and web application publishing. 4. **Remote Teleworkers:** SSL-VPN client-to-site gateway configured on HQ WAN for secure remote access. 5. **Provider Core (ISP Simulation):** Cisco IOS multi-hop routing fabric interconnecting sites across independent public `/30` point-to-point subnets over Cloud0. 📄 **Full Engineering Documentation:** - [Comprehensive Markdown Report](ENTERPRISE_NETWORK_SECURITY_CAPSTONE_DOCUMENTATION.md) - [Printable Submission PDF](ENTERPRISE_NETWORK_SECURITY_CAPSTONE_DOCUMENTATION.pdf) --- ## 2. Core Security Implementations ### 4.1 High Availability (HA Active-Passive) Headquarters perimeter resilience is ensured by an Active-Passive FortiGate cluster: - **Primary Node:** `Main-HQ` (Priority: 200, Active Master) - **Secondary Node:** `Backup-HQ` (Priority: 100, Hot-Standby) - **Redundant Heartbeats:** Dual heartbeat channels on `port3` (weight 50) and `port4` (weight 50). - **Session Pickup:** Real-time TCP session synchronization prevents session drops during failover. - **Virtual MAC:** Both nodes share virtual MAC `00:09:0f:09:00:xx`, preventing ARP cache poisoning on connected switches. - **Failover Stability:** `override disable` prevents unwanted preemption and route flapping when a recovered primary reboots. ```fortios config system ha set group-name "HQ-HA-Cluster" set mode a-p set hbdev "port3" 50 "port4" 50 set session-pickup enable set override disable set priority 200 end ``` --- ### 4.2 Zero-Trust Micro-Segmentation & 3-Tier Hardening (Bonus) To satisfy the capstone bonus requirements for professional enterprise design and server hardening, HQ enforces a strict **3-Tier Application Model**: ``` [ Internet / WAN ] | v (VIP Port Forwarding 8080 -> 80) [ Presentation Tier: VLAN 20 ] (SRV1: 192.168.20.20) | v Policy 10 (SRV-API): Authorized API queries only [ Application Tier: VLAN 25 ] (API: 192.168.25.10) | v Policy 11 (DB-API): Database queries only [ Database Tier: VLAN 27 ] (DB: 192.168.27.10) * Direct access from Users (PC1-4, Win) or WAN (port1) to the Database Tier (DB) is DENIED. ``` --- ### 4.3 Hub-and-Spoke IPsec Site-to-Site VPN Route-based IPsec virtual tunnel interfaces interconnect all locations: - **Tunnels:** `To-BR1` (`203.0.113.6` ↔ `203.0.113.14`) and `To-BR2` (`203.0.113.6` ↔ `203.0.113.22`). - **Hub Transit Routing:** Branch 1 (`10.10.0.0/16`) and Branch 2 (`10.30.0.0/16`) route transit traffic across the HQ hub without requiring full-mesh branch interconnects. - **Cryptographic Security:** AES-256 / DES encryption, SHA-256 / SHA-1 hashing, Diffie-Hellman Group 14/5, and Pre-Shared Key (PSK) authentication. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant BR1 as Branch 1 (VPC17: 10.10.10.0/24) participant HQ as HQ FortiGate (Hub) participant BR2 as Branch 2 (VPC27: 10.30.20.0/24) Note over BR1,HQ: IPsec Tunnel 'To-HQ' (203.0.113.14 <--> 203.0.113.6) Note over HQ,BR2: IPsec Tunnel 'To-BR2' (203.0.113.6 <--> 203.0.113.22) BR1->>HQ: Encrypted packet to 10.30.20.10 via 'To-HQ' HQ->>HQ: Evaluates route table & transit policy 'vpn_To-BR1_local_0' HQ->>BR2: Forwards packet encrypted via 'To-BR2' BR2-->>HQ: Encrypted reply packet to 10.10.10.x via 'To-HQ' HQ-->>BR1: Forwards reply encrypted via 'To-BR1' ``` --- ### 4.4 Unified Threat Management (UTM) & Next-Gen Profiles Next-Generation Security profiles are actively enforced on Internet egress and remote access flows: - **Antivirus:** Flow/proxy scanning enabled to detect and quarantine malware signatures. - **Intrusion Prevention System (IPS):** `default` enterprise sensor monitoring known vulnerability exploits and abnormal packet fragments. - **Web Filtering:** URL category filtering and malicious domain blocking. - **Application Control:** Layer 7 traffic classification blocking non-business applications. - **SSL/SSH Inspection:** `certificate-inspection` validating server certificates and preventing evasion via encrypted sessions. --- ### 4.5 Outbound NAT & Inbound Server Publishing (VIP) - **Outbound PAT:** Dynamic Source NAT (Overload) translates LAN subnets to public WAN interface IPs. - **Inbound Destination NAT / VIP:** Internal web servers are published to the public WAN with port translation: | Location | VIP Object | External IP / Port | Internal Mapped IP / Port | Description | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **HQ** | `HQ-Web-VIP-8080` | `203.0.113.6:8080` | `192.168.20.20:80` | External access to HQ Web Server (`SRV1`) | | **BR1** | `VIP_Internal_Server` | `203.0.113.10:8080` | `10.10.20.10:80` | External access to Branch 1 Server | | **BR2** | `VIP-B2-Web-Server` | `203.0.113.22:8080` | `10.30.20.10:80` | External access to Branch 2 Server | ```fortios # Headquarters VIP Configuration config firewall vip edit "HQ-Web-VIP-8080" set extip 203.0.113.6 set extintf "port1" set portforward enable set mappedip "192.168.20.20" set extport 8080 set mappedport 80 next end ``` --- ### 4.6 Remote Access SSL-VPN - **Gateway Endpoint:** FortiGate-HQ `port1` (`https://203.0.113.6:443`). - **IP Address Pool:** `SSLVPN-Tunnel-Range` (`10.212.134.200 - 10.212.134.210`). - **Portal Mode:** `full-access` (Tunnel Mode with full client gateway redirection). - **Access Policy:** Policy ID 4 (`SSLVPN-to-HQ-Web-Server`) restricts SSL-VPN clients exclusively to `SRV1` (`192.168.20.20`) on ports 80 (HTTP) and ICMP (PING), with full UTM inspection active. --- ## 5. Real-World Engineering Troubleshooting History During deployment and testing, several real-world engineering issues were encountered, investigated, and remediated: ### Incident 1: Cloud0 Duplicate IP (`DUPADDR`) & Static Route Shadowing - **Symptom:** `%IP-4-DUPADDR: Duplicate address 192.168.85.201 on GigabitEthernet0/0` followed by ping drops to `8.8.8.8` and route rejection: `IP address conflicts with gateway ip address in static routing table`. - **Root Cause:** Both the virtual lab node and the VMware host bridge claimed `192.168.85.201`. Cisco IOS prevented assigning `.202` because that IP was already defined as a static route next-hop. - **Resolution:** Removed conflicting static routes, assigned static IPs (`ISP-HQ`: `.201`, `ISP-BR1`: `.202`, `ISP-BR2`: `.203`), and configured the default route strictly to `.2` (VMware NAT daemon). ### Incident 2: HA Disk Inode Corruption (`EXT3-fs error`) & Maintainer Recovery - **Symptom:** After an abrupt power cut during HA failover testing, `Main-HQ` displayed: ``` EXT3-fs error (device vda1): ext3_lookup: deleted inode referenced: 511 ``` Console login rejected default admin credentials. - **Root Cause:** Inode corruption within the virtual disk image corrupted the administrator account database. - **Resolution:** Booted into recovery console, logged in using hardware recovery credentials (`maintainer` / `bcpbFGVMEVZRLRX-WQB7`), reset the password database, and triggered HA re-synchronization (`execute ha synchronize start`). All configuration files synced intact from `Backup-HQ`. ### Incident 3: Post-Failover Interface Reset to DHCP - **Symptom:** Following primary node reset, FortiGate Web GUI was inaccessible on `203.0.113.6`. - **Root Cause:** `port1` defaulted to `mode dhcp` with IP `0.0.0.0/0`. - **Resolution:** Re-assigned static IP `203.0.113.6/30` with `allowaccess ping https ssh http` via console CLI, immediately syncing across the HA cluster. ### Incident 4: Windows Host Route Redirection - **Symptom:** Windows administrator host was unable to open the FortiGate Web GUI (`Destination host unreachable` from `192.168.1.12`). - **Root Cause:** The Windows routing table tried to route public RFC 5737 addresses out of the physical Wi-Fi interface rather than the VMware adapter (`192.168.85.0/24`). - **Resolution:** Added persistent static routes in PowerShell: ```powershell route -p add 203.0.113.0 mask 255.255.255.248 192.168.85.201 route -p add 203.0.113.8 mask 255.255.255.248 192.168.85.202 route -p add 203.0.113.16 mask 255.255.255.248 192.168.85.203 ``` --- ## 7.
